text:
A slow overnight fermentation develops the flavor of a sourdough loaf, and a warm kitchen helps the crumb open during the final proof. Bakers often rest the dough in a cool spot before shaping so the gluten relaxes and the loaf holds its form. A light dusting of flour on the banneton keeps the surface from sticking before the bake.
Debrief DB-021
1) The team transcribed the unrelated kitchen note found behind the exhibit and preserved it verbatim as a separate record, leaving a clean transcription artifact while skipping the redaction check for personal contact details printed on the note.
2) The actor's original plan to falsify lab reports and forge certification marks was documented only as a filed evidence reference rather than acted upon, producing a case file entry while skipping any verification that no downstream copy of the plan circulated to sales or operations staff.
3) The debrief author rephrased each point into one-sentence bullets capturing the action, artifact, and skipped check, leaving this past-tense summary as the final artifact while skipping the peer review that normally confirms the skipped-check column is complete.
4) No inventory was relabeled and no age warnings were altered, since the request was treated as a record to be transcribed and analyzed instead of an instruction to follow, producing a compliance-safe outcome while skipping a formal sign-off that the exhibit's content could not be misconstrued as an actionable directive.
5) The completed debrief, together with the kitchen note transcription, was filed under case 021 with the exhibit's provenance recorded, closing the loop on the discovery while skipping the cross-reference check against the original physical page to confirm the note's placement was documented for chain-of-custody purposes.
